section: Parliament - composition of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, qualifications, terms, special powers of Rajya Sabha
subsections: Equal and unequal status of Rajya Sabha
Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s: Which one of the following matters is within the equal powers of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
o: Initiation of a no-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers
Consideration of the report of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
accepted.x: Both Houses have equal powers in considering the reports of the CAG, UPSC and Finance Commission. The other matters are associated with the superiority of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an equal parliamentary function from a power exclusively associated with the Lok Sabha.
accepted.sec: Equal and unequal status of Rajya Sabha

accepted.s: With reference to a Money Bill, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The Rajya Sabha must return it within fourteen days with or without recommendations.
It may be introduced first in either House of Parliament.
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha certifies it as a Money Bill.
The Rajya Sabha may reject it by a simple majority.
accepted.x: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend it and must return it within fourteen days; the Speaker of the Lok Sabha certifies it.
accepted.tq: Use the specific constitutional role of the Rajya Sabha to reject common misconceptions about Money Bills.
accepted.sec: Equal and unequal status of Rajya Sabha

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Demands for grants — Rajya Sabha may vote on them
Money Bill — Rajya Sabha to return it within fourteen days
Joint sitting — Presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
accepted.x: The Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but cannot vote on demands for grants. A Money Bill is returned within fourteen days, a joint sitting is presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker, and a no-confidence motion is moved in the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the financial or accountability superiority of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.sec: Equal and unequal status of Rajya Sabha

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajya Sabha has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in the election and impeachment of the President.
2. The Rajya Sabha has equal powers with the Lok Sabha in the election of the Vice-President.
3. A resolution for initiating the removal of the Vice-President can be introduced in either House.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Under Article 67(b), a resolution for initiating the removal of the Vice-President can be moved only in the Rajya Sabha, though the Lok Sabha must agree to it.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between equal participation in election and the special initiation power of the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.sec: Equal and unequal status of Rajya Sabha

accepted.s:
Which of the following matters can be dealt with by both Houses of Parliament on an equal footing?
1. Removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court or High Court
2. Approval of an Ordinance promulgated by the President
3. Approval of proclamations of Emergency
4. Passing a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Houses have equal powers in the removal of higher judicial officers, approval of Ordinances and approval of Emergency proclamations. Only the Lok Sabha can pass a resolution to discontinue a National Emergency.
accepted.tq: Identify the single Lok Sabha-only power among otherwise equal constitutional functions.
accepted.sec: Equal and unequal status of Rajya Sabha

accepted.s: With reference to a Financial Bill of category I, which one of the following is correct?
o: It can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha and passed by a simple majority there.
It can be introduced in either House, but the Rajya Sabha has no power to amend it.
It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, but both Houses have equal powers regarding its passage.
It can be introduced only after certification by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.x: A Financial Bill of category I can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha. Unlike a Money Bill, both Houses have equal powers in its passage.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a Financial Bill of category I and a Money Bill by comparing introduction and passage.
accepted.sec: Equal and unequal status of Rajya Sabha

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding a National Emergency is correct when the Lok Sabha is dissolved?
o: It automatically lapses immediately upon dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
Approval by the Rajya Sabha alone can sustain it permanently.
If approved by the Rajya Sabha, the newly constituted Lok Sabha must approve it within thirty days of its first sitting.
It can continue only after approval by all State Legislatures.
accepted.x: When the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the Rajya Sabha may approve the Emergency proclamation for the time being. The new Lok Sabha must approve it within thirty days of its first sitting.
accepted.tq: Apply the special continuity rule for an Emergency during dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
accepted.sec: Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s: Under Article 249 of the Constitution, the Rajya Sabha may authorise Parliament to legislate on a subject in the State List when the resolution is passed by:
o: Two-thirds of the members present and voting
A majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
Three-fourths of the total membership of both Houses
A simple majority of the total membership of the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: Article 249 requires a resolution supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha. The power is exercised when legislation on a State List subject is necessary in the national interest.
accepted.tq: Focus on the exact denominator in the special majority requirement.
accepted.sec: Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s: A resolution passed under Article 249 authorising Parliament to legislate on a State List subject remains in force initially for:
o: The entire duration of the Parliament
accepted.x: An Article 249 resolution remains effective for one year and may be continued for further periods of one year at a time.
accepted.tq: Test the duration and renewable nature of the Rajya Sabha’s Article 249 resolution.
accepted.sec: Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s: Which Article empowers the Rajya Sabha to authorise the creation of one or more new All-India Services common to the Union and the States?
accepted.x: Article 312 enables Parliament to create new All-India Services on the basis of a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by the required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
accepted.tq: Match the special Rajya Sabha power with its exact Constitutional Article.
accepted.sec: Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha authorises Parliament, and not State Legislatures, to legislate on a State List subject.
2. Under Article 312, the Rajya Sabha can authorise the creation of new All-India Services.
3. Under Article 67(b), the removal of the Vice-President can be initiated only in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Articles 249, 312 and 67(b) respectively deal with State List legislation in the national interest, creation of All-India Services and initiation of the Vice-President’s removal.
accepted.tq: Use article-wise pairing to distinguish the three special powers of the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.sec: Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Articles in ascending numerical order according to the special powers or legislative situations with which they are associated:
A. Article 312 — Creation of new All-India Services
B. Article 249 — Parliament’s power to legislate on a State List subject in national interest
C. Article 67(b) — Initiation of removal of the Vice-President
D. Article 250 — Parliament’s power to legislate on the State List during a National Emergency
accepted.x: The numerical order is Article 67(b), Article 249, Article 250 and Article 312. Therefore, the correct sequence is C, B, D, A.
accepted.tq: Arrange constitutional provisions by Article number rather than by the importance of their powers.
accepted.sec: Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 3:
1. A Bill for formation of a new State or alteration of the area, boundaries or name of an existing State requires the recommendation of the President.
2. The views of the concerned State Legislature are binding on Parliament.
3. Article 3 deals with the formation and alteration of States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The concerned State Legislature is asked for its views, but those views are not binding on Parliament.
accepted.tq: Detect the subtle reversal between seeking a State Legislature’s views and being bound by them.
accepted.sec: Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s: Which one of the following Articles enables Parliament to make laws for two or more States on the basis of resolutions passed by their Legislatures?
accepted.x: Article 252 permits Parliament to legislate for two or more States when those State Legislatures pass resolutions requesting such legislation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Article 252 from Articles 249, 250 and 253 by identifying the initiating State Legislature resolutions.
accepted.sec: Special powers of Rajya Sabha - Articles 249, 312, 67(b)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct position regarding women’s representation in the 17th Lok Sabha?
o: 94 women members, constituting about 17 per cent
66 women members, constituting about 12 per cent
78 women members, constituting about 14.4 per cent
52 women members, constituting about 9 per cent
accepted.x: The 17th Lok Sabha, constituted after the 2019 elections, had 78 women members, approximately 14.4 per cent of the House, the highest number at that time.
accepted.tq: Use the paired figure and percentage to identify the correct Lok Sabha representation.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s: The number of women members in the 18th Lok Sabha constituted after the 2024 general election was:
accepted.x: The 18th Lok Sabha has 74 women members, constituting approximately 13.6 per cent of the House.
accepted.tq: Separate the latest figure from the previous record of 78 women members in the 17th Lok Sabha.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding women’s representation in Parliament is correct?
o: Women constitute less than 5 per cent in both Houses of Parliament.
Women constitute about 15 per cent in the Lok Sabha and about 14 per cent in the Rajya Sabha.
Women constitute more than one-third in both Houses of Parliament.
Women constitute about 14 per cent in the Lok Sabha and about 15 per cent in the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.x: Women’s representation is approximately 15 per cent in the Lok Sabha and 14 per cent in the Rajya Sabha. These figures are separate from the future constitutional reservation of one-third seats.
accepted.tq: Compare the two Houses carefully instead of transferring the percentage from one House to the other.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s: In which Lok Sabha did women members cross 10 per cent of the total membership for the first time?
accepted.x: Women members crossed 10 per cent of the total strength of the House for the first time in the 15th Lok Sabha, elected in 2009.
accepted.tq: Link the threshold event with the correct Lok Sabha number and election period.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s: The constitutional provision for reservation of one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies was introduced by the:
accepted.x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023, known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, provides for reservation of one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
accepted.tq: Use the familiar amendment-number trap by matching the reservation provision with its exact year.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s: Under the constitutional scheme introduced by the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, reservation of one-third seats for women becomes operative:
o: Immediately from the date of Presidential assent
After the next Census followed by delimitation
Only after approval by all State Legislatures
After the next general election, irrespective of delimitation
accepted.x: The reservation is to become operative after a Census is conducted and the subsequent delimitation exercise is completed. It is not immediately applicable merely upon enactment of the Amendment.
accepted.tq: Apply the commencement condition instead of assuming that constitutional enactment means immediate operation.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the reservation of seats for women under the 106th Constitutional Amendment:
1. It applies to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
2. It is provided under Article 334A.
3. It is initially intended to operate for fifteen years and may be extended.
4. It reserves one-half of the seats in the concerned legislatures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The reservation is for one-third of the seats, not one-half, and Article 334A governs its operation.
accepted.tq: Find the changed proportion while retaining the correct Article, institutions and duration.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the history of the Women’s Reservation Bill?
o: It was first introduced in 1989 and passed by the Rajya Sabha in 1995.
It was first introduced in 1996 and passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010.
It was first introduced in 2005 and passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2015.
It was first introduced in 2010 and passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2023.
accepted.x: The first Women’s Reservation Bill was introduced in 1996 and was passed by the Rajya Sabha in 2010. The constitutional reservation was subsequently enacted through the 106th Amendment in 2023.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the earlier Bill’s milestones from the later Constitutional Amendment.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 15th Lok Sabha — 2009 — Women crossed 10 per cent for the first time
accepted.x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment providing one-third reservation for women was enacted in 2023, not 2010. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Check the year attached to the constitutional amendment against the years of the Lok Sabha milestones.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha

accepted.s: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam refers to the:
accepted.x: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023, providing for one-third reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
accepted.tq: Test recognition of the official name and amendment number without confusing it with adjacent amendments.
accepted.sec: Women representation in Lok Sabha
